findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: 5302461_full_platform_role_gates_and_approved_predicates.sql:29-70 recreates notifications_insert_system_or_admin and the three document_shares policies with public.user_has_role and the full platform key set; node scripts/verify-rls.mjs now reports 0 warnings (the '[role-gate:baseline]' line is gone).

findings.title: notifications INSERT policy allows any authenticated user to write a self-addressed row into an arbitrary organization
findings.note: NEW at 6b7aa1a5: the self branch of 5302461:29-37 is only `user_id = auth.uid()`; unlike the admin branch it does not require approved membership in notifications.organization_id. A user with the anon key + their JWT (the PostgREST path the RLS policies exist for) can insert a notification row tagged with another tenant's organization_id, as long as the user_id is their own. Impact is bounded (the row is only selectable by the same user and no current org-wide notification read path was found), but it is a cross-tenant write into another tenant's dataset that will pollute any future org-scoped reporting or admin query.

report: Read-only re-verification at 6b7aa1a5; no hosted-Supabase or local-Postgres replay. 13 of 17 previous RLS rows verified fixed, 4 partially fixed, 0 regressed, 1 new P3. Executed: node scripts/verify-rls.mjs (140/140 tables RLS-enabled, 1035 policies, 0 failures, 0 warnings), node scripts/check-rls-predicate.mjs (PASS, 34 migrations), node scripts/check-permission-catalog.mjs (PASS: 206 route + 46 policy references vs 338 keys), and promtool check/test rules against prom/prometheus:v3.5.1 (26 rules, tests SUCCESS). 5302461 closes both RLS-P3-008 and the pre-baseline notifications exception; 5302452/5302447/5302448/5302435/5302436 remain effective. Residuals: service-role fallback + secret-defined allow-lists (RLS-P2-004), no anon-grant lint (RLS-P3-001), name-derived storage org (RLS-P3-003), unguarded matrix counts (RLS-P3-004).
